- The Impact of Our Graduates on Society

In 2022, we were filled with positive energy by the stories of our graduates' contributions in various sectors of society. Through them, we extend our legacy.

In the business field, the reputation they provide and the leadership they exercise are some of the achievements of this community that already reaches 61,709 people.

These EAFIT alumni are part of a network that continues to demonstrate its ability to transform society. This is confirmed by news such as the graduates' leadership in startups highlighted by Forbes magazine as among the best in Colombia; the inclusion of three graduates on Forbes' list of the 50 most powerful women in the country; engineer Sara Rengifo's contribution to NASA's Artemis mission; the appointment of musician Ana María Patiño as the first female assistant conductor of the Orchestre Suisse Romande; and the philanthropic contributions and initiatives spearheaded by this community, among other milestones that fill us with EAFIT pride.

#### **Sara Rengifo helped push the future forward in NASA's mission to the Moon**

## Excellence and recognition

This Mechanical Engineering program at EAFIT focuses on studying the materials required for space missions and investigating life support and environmental control systems at the Marshall Space Flight Center, one of the research and development facilities involved in Artemis, the US space agency's project that aims to send people to the Moon in 2024 and launched its first mission on November 16, 2022.

¡Sara Rengifo, una eafitense que ayuda a empujar el futuro en la misión de [@nasa\_es](https://www.instagram.com/nasa_es/?utm_source=ig_embed) \_es a la Luna 🌜!

[@sararengifo](https://www.instagram.com/sararengifo/?utm_source=ig_embed) es ingeniera mecánica de la Escuela de [@cienciasingenieriaeafit](https://www.instagram.com/cienciasingenieriaeafit/?utm_source=ig_embed) , está en el [@nasakennedy](https://www.instagram.com/nasakennedy/?utm_source=ig_embed) pendiente del desarrollo de la misión 𝗔𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗶𝘀 𝗜, que hará este sábado el segundo intento de lanzamiento del cohete Space Launch System (SLS). Ella se ocupa de estudiar 🧐 materiales que se requieren para las misiones espaciales 🌌 desde los laboratorios de Tribología y Metrología del [@nasa\_marshall](https://www.instagram.com/nasa_marshall/?utm_source=ig_embed), uno de los 14 centros de la Agencia Espacial involucrados en Artemis, el proyecto que pretende llevar al hombre al satélite en el año 2024 🚀.

💫 Otro de los proyectos en los que trabaja Sara es Enviromental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS), que se encarga de reciclar el vapor, el sudor o la orina para hacer posible la vida de los astronautas 🧑‍🚀 en la Estación Espacial Internacional.

Sara está en 📍 Cabo Cañaveral pendiente del que ella llama “el bebé de [@nasa](https://www.instagram.com/nasa/?utm_source=ig_embed) ” y “el cohete 🚀 más potente que ha creado la humanidad”. Desde allí, a dos días del segundo intento de lanzamiento de Artemis I, la egresada de Ingeniería Mecánica de [#EAFIT](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/EAFIT/?utm_source=ig_embed) nos comparte detalles de la misión.

#### **We are delivering to society the first cohort of undergraduate students in Literature**

## Regionalization, internationalization and projection

On July 14, the University presented society with nine EAFIT graduates who formed the first cohort of the undergraduate program in Literature at the School of Arts and Humanities. These writers contribute new narratives that, through art and culture, also transform the world.
